examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Probability of a Complement
examples.problem: Given that $P(B)=0.6,$ $P(A\cap B)=0.4,$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.9,$ find $P(A').$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.9 & =P(A)+0.6-0.4 \\ P(A) & =0.9+0.4-0.6 \\ P(A) & =0.7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P({A}^{′}) & =1-P(A) \\  & =1-0.7 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
